title: How to connect your PADI card to book dives in Hurghada
body_markdown:
Show up at a Hurghada dive center with only a paper certification card from a course you took eight years ago, and you'll spend your first morning explaining eLearning completion dates instead of getting in the water. Connect your PADI card to your dive booking before you land, and the dive team verifies your level in under a minute, no scanning old photos, no phone calls to a dive shop in another country.


**TL;DR**

- Add your PADI digital card and certification number to your Daily Red Sea booking before arrival to skip in-person verification delays.
- Open Water Diver certifies dives to 18 meters; Advanced Open Water extends that to 30 meters across 5 adventure dives.
- No PADI card yet? Book a Discover Scuba Diving session in Hurghada with no prior certification required.
- Lost or unissued cards are the top booking blocker — the PADI app digital card fixes this in most cases within minutes.
- Certified divers with logged dives in the last 12 months skip the refresher; anyone else should plan for a short requalification dive.


## Why this matters

Dive centers in Hurghada legally have to confirm certification level before letting anyone descend past entry-level depths. That check used to mean emailing a scanned card photo days ahead or arriving early to sort it out at the counter.

With the PADI app's digital card and a booking form that asks for it upfront, the verification step happens before you touch sand. That means the difference between a 7am dive boat departure and a delayed one while staff track down your paperwork.

Getting [PADI certified in Hurghada](https://dailyredsea.byryze.com/how-to-get-padi-certified-while-in-hurghada) is straightforward if you're starting from zero, but this guide is for divers who already hold a card and want the booking side connected correctly the first time.

## Before you start

- **A PADI account** tied to the email or phone number used during your original certification course — this is what the PADI app pulls your card from.
- **Your certification number and level** (Open Water, Advanced Open Water, Rescue Diver, etc.) plus the date of your last logged dive, since some centers ask for recency, not just level.
- **The gotcha:** if your course finished within the last few days, your card may not be digitally issued yet. PADI processing after course completion can lag, so book your first Hurghada dive with a few days of buffer rather than the morning you land.

## Set up your PADI account access

1. Open the **PADI app** (or padi.com) and sign in with the account used when you certified.
2. Tap **My Certifications** or the card icon on the home screen.
3. Confirm your card shows your correct **certification level** and **certification date** — this is the exact data a dive shop needs.
4. If your card isn't listed, use the **Find My Certification** lookup tool inside the app with your name and approximate course date.

Expected result: your PADI digital card is visible and shows the correct level before you touch a booking form.

## Add your certification to a booking

1. On the Daily Red Sea booking page for your chosen dive trip, look for the **certification details** field.
2. Enter your **PADI certification number** exactly as shown on your digital card, no spaces added.
3. Select your **certification level** from the dropdown — this determines which dive sites and depths you're eligible for.
4. Note your **last dive date** in the same field or message box; centers use this to flag divers who need a supervised refresher.
5. Submit the booking and keep the confirmation message; you'll show the same certification number at check-in.

Expected result: your booking confirmation lists your certification level next to the trip name, which is what the dive team checks against your card on the day.


![Four steps from opening the PADI app to verifying at check-in](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/7a6dd8e9-ac74-4545-89b4-7263579c0db6/body-7c657bd4c8b603c5860b0709a3442d19.jpg)

*The whole process runs before you reach the boat, not on the dock.*


## Verify with the dive team

1. Arrive with either the **PADI app open** on your phone or a printed copy of your digital card.
2. Hand over your **certification number** and a photo ID matching the name on the card.
3. The dive team cross-checks your level against the trip you booked — Open Water divers are held to the 18-meter limit; Advanced Open Water divers can go to 30 meters.
4. If your last dive was more than 12 months ago, expect a short **refresher or check-out dive** before the main trip, standard PADI practice regardless of which dive operator you book with.

Expected result: your card matches your booking, and you board the boat without a paperwork delay.

## Booking without a PADI card yet

Not every diver arrives with a card. If you've never certified, book a **Discover Scuba Diving** session instead of a certified-diver trip — no PADI number required, and an instructor stays with you the entire dive. The [scuba diving courses for complete beginners in Hurghada](https://dailyredsea.byryze.com/scuba-diving-courses-for-complete-beginners-in-hurghada) page covers what a first-timer session actually involves before you commit.

Divers who did the classroom and pool sessions elsewhere but never finished open-water dives can complete a **referral dive** in Hurghada instead of restarting the whole course — check with your original instructor for a referral form before booking.

## Troubleshooting

- **Card shows the wrong level.** This usually means two certifications are linked to different PADI accounts. Use the app's **Find My Certification** tool with both possible emails.
- **Card not issued yet.** Recently completed courses can take a few days to process. Book your Hurghada dive with buffer days, not the day after finishing a course elsewhere.
- **Certification number rejected at check-in.** Double-check for a transposed digit — PADI numbers are long, and a single typo in the booking form causes this every time.
- **No dives logged in over a year.** Expect a required refresher dive before deeper trips; this isn't optional and isn't specific to any one operator.
- **Lost physical card, no app account.** Recreate your account using the email from your original certifying dive shop, then run the lookup tool.

## Customize your workflow

Once your PADI card connects cleanly to a booking, the next move is picking the right trip for your level. Certified divers ready for deeper sites can move straight into [certified diver trips in Hurghada](https://dailyredsea.byryze.com/scuba-diving-for-certified-divers-in-hurghada), while anyone chasing the 30-meter depth range should look at the [Advanced Open Water course](https://dailyredsea.byryze.com/advanced-open-water-diver-course-in-hurghada) before booking wreck or drift sites that require it.

If you're arranging dives around flights and hotel transfers, confirming a booking through WhatsApp keeps the whole trip in one thread instead of scattered emails.

## FAQ


**How do I connect my PADI card to a Hurghada dive booking?**

Enter your PADI certification number and level in the booking form's certification field, then bring the PADI app or a printed card to check-in for verification.

**Can I book a dive in Hurghada without a PADI card?**

Yes, book a Discover Scuba Diving session, which requires no prior certification and pairs you with an instructor for the entire dive.

**What depth can Open Water divers reach in Hurghada?**

PADI Open Water Diver certification allows dives to 18 meters. Advanced Open Water Diver extends that limit to 30 meters.

**What if my PADI card hasn't been issued yet?**

Recently completed courses can take a few days to process in the PADI system, so book your Hurghada dive with buffer days rather than immediately after finishing a course.

**Do I need a refresher dive if I haven't dived in a while?**

Divers without a logged dive in the past 12 months typically need a short supervised refresher before joining a deeper trip, standard practice across PADI-affiliated operators.

**What's the difference between Advanced Open Water and Rescue Diver certification?**

Advanced Open Water covers 5 adventure dives that expand your depth range and skills, while Rescue Diver focuses on emergency response and diver safety, usually taken after Advanced.

**Can I use a referral dive to finish certification in Hurghada?**

Yes, if you completed classroom and pool sessions elsewhere, bring a referral form from your original instructor to finish open-water dives in Hurghada.

**How do I find my PADI certification if I lost my card?**

Use the Find My Certification tool inside the PADI app or on padi.com with your name and approximate course date to relink your account.


## One last thing

The single biggest delay divers hit in Hurghada isn't the dive site or the boat schedule — it's a certification card that was never digitized after an old course, sitting in a filing cabinet somewhere instead of an app. Fix that once in 2026 and every booking after it moves faster.
